> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 079deea822a0bba4d7cfff58acb55eaaad58add0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `220dfce3d4eccba6ffb43686df31eb3177432c9a` — the merge of head `7c5ee8b24eb602bec66f40b3c0113734c95b7cba` into base `079deea822a0bba4d7cfff58acb55eaaad58add0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 220dfce3d4eccba6ffb43686df31eb3177432c9a && git checkout 220dfce3d4eccba6ffb43686df31eb3177432c9a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 079deea822a0bba4d7cfff58acb55eaaad58add0 7c5ee8b24eb602bec66f40b3c0113734c95b7cba && git checkout -B drift-repro 079deea822a0bba4d7cfff58acb55eaaad58add0 && git merge --no-ff 7c5ee8b24eb602bec66f40b3c0113734c95b7cba

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 079deea822a0bba4d7cfff58acb55eaaad58add0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 079deea822a0bba4d7cfff58acb55eaaad58add0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `25f758a5e43c80bb0ba4e0b7754f23cc6745f5cc`
Local-runs: none

PR #26662 (card #26583, ruling 6439306670 letter A, claim 6440220432, dev report 6441342414), reviewed on the declaration face at 2026-10-27T12:12Z. Inputs: the card body and its five comments, the PR body and file list, `git diff origin/main...25f758a5e` (7 files, +329/−26, merge-base `c739de755c`), cited code read with `git show 25f758a5e:PATH`, and the head's check-runs. Rendered by the seat's subagent.

Scope (TIER_DEFAULT, whole diff): `.changeset/26583-print-named-page.md`, `content/docs/ui/print-pages.mdx`, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/print-named-page.fixture.ts`, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/print-service-named-page.dogfood.test.ts`, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/print-service-render.dogfood.test.ts`, `packages/services/service-print/src/print-service.test.ts`, `packages/services/service-print/src/print-service.ts`. No `packages/spec/**`, no governed path, no ADR: the committed tree carries no schema face and no rules face, so the tier is the one the `Clause-②: yes` line alone owes.

**Gate verdicts on this head, as read at 2026-10-27T12:12Z** (47 check-runs): 21 `success`, 10 `skipped`, 14 `cancelled`, 2 `failure`. The two failures are the aggregates `TypeScript Type Check` and `Lint & Repo Gates`, whose only failed step is "Verify every … lane succeeded", started 2026-10-27T12:04Z, one minute after the dev pushed `7c5ee8b24e` to the branch at 2026-10-27T12:03Z: the workflow's concurrency cancel took the lanes (`Test Core` 1–6/8, `Build Docs`, every `Type Check ·` lane, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`) and the aggregates then reported the missing lanes as failure. No lane failed on its own. Green on this head: `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Test Core` 7/8 and 8/8, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Auto Label`, `filter`, `Test UI`. So the derived type-check, lint and test-core families have NO conclusion on `25f758a5e`; on the newer head `7c5ee8b24e` (same diff plus a 4+/3− docblock in `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/invoice-document.page.ts`) they read 30 `success`, 10 `skipped`, 5 `in_progress`, 0 failures at the same minute. The dev's local run of the derived subset at `25f758a5e`: 88 of 89 families exit 0, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured (CI's). The seat adopts this record on `7c5ee8b24e` once its lanes finish, or re-renders; nothing in this record depends on the one-comment delta.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, read in the cited code:

1. **The page refusal narrows to two arms — right.** `refuseUnlessPrintPage` (`print-service.ts:379–400`) keeps `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`/404 for an unknown name, then `VALIDATION_ERROR`/400 unless `isRecordPageOf(page, req.object)`, then 400 unless `page.print` is set; the third arm on `main` (`defaultRecordPageObject(page) !== req.object` → 400 "is not the default record page") is deleted. This is exactly ruling A's "two loud refusals". The check still runs before the record read, the mint and the browser (step ③ of `printRecordToFile`, `print-service.ts:302–304`; the function now returns the page the URL is built from). The 400 message gains the parenthesis "(type: 'record', object: 'X')"; code and status are unchanged, so no wire vocabulary moves.

2. **Server predicate equals the console's — right, and no wider.** Server: `isRecordPageOf(page, object) = page.type === 'record' && page.object === object` (`print-service.ts:187–189`), asked only after a non-object page was refused 404 and after `validateRequest` (`:436–446`) made `req.object` a non-empty string. Console: `isRecordPageOf` in `ui/packages/react/src/hooks/usePageAssignment.ts:94–98` is the same two comparisons behind a null/empty guard the server has already satisfied; `RecordDetailView.tsx:780–792` asks it of the page found by name in `useMetadata().pages` for the named route and sets `namedPageState = 'refused'` otherwise, with no fallback (`:794–808`: a refused or pending name draws neither the resolved page nor the synthesized default). Both sides read one store: the console's list is `getMetaItems('page')` → `readFlattenedMetaItems` → `engine.registry.listItems('page')` served raw (`protocol.ts:9368–9380, 9442–9460`; no type fill on the serve side, the only fills are the save door `:20924` and stored-row hydration `:6429`), and the server reads `engine.registry.getItem('page', name)` on the `objectql` service (`print-service-plugin.ts:85`). So the set the server accepts is the set the console's named route draws: a `type: 'record'` page bound to the request's object. Note for the seat (unchanged by this PR, not a finding): on the plain record route the console picks the object's default by `defaultRecordPageObject` over its served order (`usePageAssignment.ts:205`), so under the two-defaults boundary the hook itself documents (objectstack#23213) the paper could be the other default; the ruling keeps the record route for the default page, and `main` had the same exposure.

3. **The render URL — right.** `printPageUrl` (`print-service.ts:205–210`): `CONSOLE/apps/{app}/{object}/record/{recordId}`, each segment `encodeURIComponent`-ed, is the whole URL when `defaultRecordPageObject(page) === req.object` (after check 2 that is `isDefault === true` exactly); otherwise `/page/{encodeURIComponent(req.page)}` is appended. That is the console's `RECORD_NAMED_PAGE_ROUTE = ':objectName/record/:recordId/page/:pageName'` (`AppContent.tsx:280`, mounted at `:1449` on `RecordDetailView`, beside `:objectName/record/:recordId` at `:1443`). The unit rows pin both routes and the encoding (`inv%201`, `doc%2F1`, `print-service.test.ts:408–428`); an explicit `isDefault: false` takes the named route (`:420`), which the console also draws. The filename stays `{page}-{recordId}.pdf`.

4. **Removed accept arm on `main` had no hidden width.** `main`'s first check was `page.object !== req.object` and its third required `defaultRecordPageObject(page) === req.object` (`isDefault: true`, `type` record-or-absent). So `main` already refused a `type: 'app'`/`'home'` page and a non-default page; the head's added refusal rows (`print-service.test.ts:280–288`: another object, no `print` default and non-default, `type: 'home'` default, `type: 'app'` non-default, no `type` default and non-default) describe the new set correctly. The one shape `main` accepted that the head refuses is the typeless default print page; judged in ③.

5. **Docs — right.** `content/docs/ui/print-pages.mdx` loses "A print page that is not the default is refused", says which route each page renders on, the example `InvoiceDocumentPage` drops `isDefault: true` (now a non-default print page beside a working page, which is the capability), and refusal row 3 reads "not a record page of the object (`type: 'record'`, that `object`), or declares no `print`". The repo has no translation of this page (`content/docs/ui/print-pages.mdx` is the only `print-pages*`). The duplicated row number 3 in the refusal table predates the PR.

6. **Dogfood — right, with one CI limit named.** `print-service-named-page.dogfood.test.ts` saves the brief through `protocol.saveMetaItem` (the real save door), keeps `showcase_project_detail` as the default working page with no `print`, and asserts the named URL, the archive as the requester, the 400 for the working page and the 400 for the brief asked of `showcase_invoice`, nothing minted on either. `print-service-render.dogfood.test.ts` adds a real-Chromium leg on the named route; that file is skipped in CI (no console bundle), so its new leg is measured only by the dev's local run (`OS_PAGE_REACT_ENABLED=on`, PDF text "Project brief / Brief / PROJECT NAME STATUS …"). The stand-in file runs in the `Dogfood Regression Gate`, green on this head.

7. **Changeset and declarations — right** (② below). No new export, no new key, no request-body change: `PrintRecordRequest` already carries `page`.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/26583-print-named-page.md`: `'@objectstack/service-print': patch`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in the changeset body and in the PR body. The diff publishes from one released package, `@objectstack/service-print` (`src/print-service.ts`); the docs, dogfood tests and changeset publish nothing. `Metadata-protocol: none` is measured right: no `packages/spec` edit, no key added, refused or re-meant, no default changed; `print` and `isDefault` keep their meaning and the request already names its page. `Clause-②: yes` is right: the public door `printRecordToFile` / `POST /api/v1/print/records` answers 201 where it answered 400. The arm is `(widening)` on every authoring door (③ flag 3 holds the one raw-body shape and leaves the re-arm to the seat). The level follows AGENTS.md:1091–1093: `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`; so `patch` is the right bump, and `minor` would be wrong. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — measured on the diff; the raw-body shape in ③ flag 3 is the seat's to re-arm.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none in the dev report. Three `out_of_scope_findings` and one dev-acceptance note, each answered:

1. **CSP / `unsafe-eval` on a default deployment** (class a, public door). Outside this PR: `chromium-driver.ts:303` passes `PRINT_READY_PREDICATE` as a string to `page.waitForFunction`, which the console's default policy (`packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts:851–852`, no `'unsafe-eval'` unless `OS_PAGE_REACT_ENABLED`) refuses, so every server print fails on a default environment at `main` too (the untouched invoice leg included). Not caused or widened by this diff, and not fixable inside the claim's file surface without touching the driver. Escalated to the seat for its own card (the dev reported it; it also blocks hotcrm#2312 on a default deployment even after this PR lands). It does not change this verdict.

2. **`examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/invoice-document.page.ts:12–14`** says the invoice print page is the default "because … that is the page a record prints on". Answered by the dev after this head: `7c5ee8b24e` (pushed 2026-10-27T12:03Z) rewrites that docblock, 4+/3−, no code change. It is outside the claim's file surface but on no governed path and publishes nothing (`examples/` is private). The seat adopts this record on that head or re-renders; this record names `25f758a5e` only.

3. **The typeless default print page — measured; one door class exists, and the seat decides the arm.** The shape: a registry page body with no `type`, `isDefault: true`, `object: X`, `print` set, asked for an `X` record. `main` accepted it (its third check read `defaultRecordPageObject`, which treats an absent `type` as `'record'`, `packages/spec/src/ui/default-record-page.ts:67–73`); the head refuses it 400 (`isRecordPageOf` reads `type` exactly; pinned at `print-service.test.ts:287–288`). Doors that cannot produce it, each filling `PageSchema`'s declared default (`page.zod.ts:1943`, `PAGE_TYPE_DEFAULT`): `defineStack` (`stack.zod.ts:5341ff` parses with `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse` and returns `result.data`; `pages: z.array(PageSchema)` at `:725`), so every `os build` artifact and `os validate`; the artifact loader (`packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts:1321`, `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.parse`); the metadata save door (`protocol.ts:20924`, `withDeclaredPageTypeDefault`); stored-row hydration (`protocol.ts:6429` `convertStoredItem`, which every stored-row `registerItem` at `:17861`, `:18344`, `:18908` reads through); and the file-system metadata sync, which registers no pages at all (`objectql/src/plugin.ts:3806`, `metadataTypes = ['object','view','app','flow','hook']`). Doors that CAN: (a) a manifest built in code and handed to `manifest.register()` / `ql.registerApp()` without `defineStack` (`objectql/src/plugin.ts:813`, `:1138`) → `registerMetadataCollections` (`engine.ts:8726`, `:9014`) → `registry.registerItem('page', raw)`, where the registry's page seam (`registry.ts:5307–5323`) judges `misplacedDefaultPageRefusal` and `defaultRecordPageObject` and parses nothing — the spec docblock itself names "the pages a package registers without a parse"; (b) the metadata facade `register('page', name, raw)` (`metadata-facade.ts:105–122`, no parse); (c) a raw `registry.registerItem` (the dev's case); (d) an authored package install, which stores the manifest "exactly as handed" (`protocol-package-install.ts:228` parses for declaration only; `registry.installPackage` at `registry.ts:6122ff` registers no page items) and whose pages reach the registry at the next boot through `manifestService.register()` → `registerApp` (`runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:2658`), raw. For every one of those doors the served list shows the console the same typeless body (`readFlattenedMetaItems` serves `registry.listItems` raw), so the console's record route never drew that page on `main` (its object lookup filters with `isRecordPageOf`, `usePageAssignment.ts:168`, and synthesized the default instead) and its named route refuses it: the 201 `main` answered put a different document on paper. In-repo code-registered default record pages (`sys_user`, `sys_organization`, `sys_approval_request`) all carry `type: 'record'` and declare no `print`, so no shipped page is in the shape. Reading: the set of requests that print the page they name only widens; the set of requests answered 201 loses one shape, reachable only through a raw-body door no author of a `definePage`/`defineStack`/`os build`/Studio-save page passes, and whose 201 was a misprint. The dev declared `yes (widening)` and said so in the PR body. Escalated: if the seat reads the 201→400 flip on the raw-body shape as a narrowing, the PR is re-armed `(narrowing)` and moves to the narrowing face at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER, which this record does not serve; making the server read an absent `type` as `'record'` instead would make it wider than the console and print a not-found state or a synthesized page, so that is not the fix.

4. **`print-service-render.dogfood.test.ts` is CI-skipped**, so the named-route real render is pinned only by the dev's local reading; the stand-in dogfood and the unit rows pin the URL and refusals in CI. Accepted as is: the file was CI-skipped before this PR for the same reason.

5. **Head moved during review.** The PR head is `7c5ee8b24e` since 2026-10-27T12:03Z; this record names `25f758a5e`, whose type-check, lint and test-core lanes were cancelled by that push (gate section above). The seat adopts on the newer head when its five in-progress runs conclude, or re-renders.

Seat questions, one line each:
- Predicate: yes — the server's `isRecordPageOf` is the console's two comparisons over the same registry (`usePageAssignment.ts:94–98`, asked at `RecordDetailView.tsx:780–792`), behind guards the server has already satisfied; it accepts exactly what the named route draws, no wider.
- Narrowing: a typeless page CAN enter the registry through raw-body doors — a code-built manifest via `manifest.register()`/`ql.registerApp()`, the metadata facade's `register('page', …)`, a raw `registry.registerItem`, and an authored install manifest re-registered at boot — while every parsing door (`defineStack`, artifact load, save door, stored-row hydration) fills the default; on that shape `main` printed the console's synthesized default page, not the page named, so the seat decides whether a misprinting 201 turned 400 re-arms the PR.
- URL: confirmed — `…/apps/APP/OBJECT/record/ID/page/PAGE` with every segment `encodeURIComponent`-ed, matching `RECORD_NAMED_PAGE_ROUTE`; the default page (`isDefault: true`) keeps `…/apps/APP/OBJECT/record/ID`, both pinned in the unit rows.
- Declarations: `Clause-②: yes` right, `(widening)` measured on every authoring door with flag 3 escalated, `Metadata-protocol: none` right (no spec key, value or default moves), and `patch` is the bump AGENTS.md:1091–1093 assigns to a non-protocol change.

| Shape | Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #26583` under ruling `6439306670` letter A. 8 files: `print-service.ts` and its unit test, two dogfood tests and a fixture, `print-pages.mdx`, a `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/service-print`, and one docblock in `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/invoice-document.page.ts`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` appear in both the body and the changeset. No key is added, so the card reads p2, as the PR body says. |
| Fix | `refuseUnlessPrintPage` keeps the 404 for an unknown page and two 400s: not a record page of this object, and no `print`. The default page renders the plain record route; any other print page renders `…/apps/APP/OBJECT/record/ID/page/PAGE` (`RECORD_NAMED_PAGE_ROUTE`), each segment encoded. The server's `isRecordPageOf` is the console's own predicate (`type === 'record' && object === OBJECT`) over the same registry, so the server prints exactly the pages the named route draws. |
| Head delta | `7c5ee8b24e` adds only the showcase docblock fix (4+/3−) on top of the reviewed `25f758a5e`. The seat widened the claim surface by that comment, at the dev's own out-of-scope note: the old text said the default page is the only page a record prints on, which this PR makes untrue. The contract review does not depend on it. |
| Clause-② boundary (seat call) | The review escalated one shape: a page body with no `type`, marked `isDefault: true` and declaring `print`, can reach the registry through a raw code path (a code-built manifest, `registry.registerItem`, the metadata facade) though every authoring door fills `type`'s schema default. `main` answered 201 for it but rendered the plain record route, where the console filters with the same `isRecordPageOf` and draws the synthesized default page, so that PDF was not the requested page. The head answers 400.
